text:
maya: Heads up — after today's release we see a tail-latency spike on streaming endpoints. p50 stable, p95/p99 up ~150-300ms. Happens mostly on toolcall-heavy flows. :frowning:

liam: repro on prod? any traces?

maya: yes observed in us-west region, some traces attached. quick trace snippet:
```
SSE write -> serialize toolcall frame (80ms) -> kernel select (hot path) -> flush
```

devon: saw a similar in staging this morning. CI perf job flagged `stream_latency_test` on eventsource suite.

ci-bot: perf-ci: stream_latency_test regressed on 2109-release-3, delta +220ms p99. Full profile: https://ci.internal/perf/2109...

anna: initial bisect points at merge 2109-feat/batching-heuristic-change. Rolling back that PR locally removes spike.

liam: that PR changed batch coalescing threshold + introduced a "synchronous flush" when toolcall frames present to avoid partial toolcall frames, might be forcing serialization path. Could be ordering with kv cache prefetch.

devon: tracer shows KV cache miss bursts before toolcall, causing stalls, kernel autoselect chooses single-token optimized kernel leading to many tiny kernels -> overhead.

maya: ruled out network — saw the SSE buffers growing. Looks like the runtime is buffering SSE chunks until a toolcall boundary, then serializing entire buffered chunk. That's adding 100-200ms.

anna: can someone grab a flamegraph for sse-write path with kernel sampling? `perf record -g -p <pid>` should show.

liam: I ran a lightweight perf in staging. Paste:
```
samples:
  sse_write: 45%
  serialize_toolcall: 30%
  kernel_selector: 15%
  kv_prefetch: 10%
```

devon: suggestion: revert synchronous flush flag and instead emit toolcall markers as separate SSE messages so we don't force full serialization. Also tweak batch heuristic to avoid switching to single-token kernel when kv-prefetch next tokens are pending.

maya: agree. But revert is risky mid-release. Could we do a targeted canary rollback for the heuristic only?

anna: opened a rollback PR that toggles `enable_sync_toolcall_flush=false` for canary nodes. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4321

liam: run a quick A/B in us-west-canary. If p99 drops back, confirm rollout hold.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for us-west-canary (nodes: 3). monitoring dashboards: https://mon.internal/d/us-west-canary

devon: also add short-lived metric: sse_buffer_hold_ms per request and toolcall_serialize_ms.

maya: thanks — adding alerts for sse_buffer_hold_ms > 50ms.

liam: if canary looks good, we can either revert PR or implement emitting markers fix. Which is faster?

anna: revert + revert PR is fastest for immediate mitigation. Engineer time to implement markers ~2 days.

maya: agree, let's revert for now, then follow up with markers+heuristic fixes.

liam: I'll prepare emergency revert PR and coordinate with infra for fast canary promotion.

maya: thanks. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
